parsed.why: State protections actively operate—facilities, non-discrimination, hate-crime enforcement, custody consent decree, safe-passage—but national passport/screening/federal custody exposure caps safety.
Birth-sex custody placement with documented sexual assault and courts dismissing relief is severe state failure; hostile sex-definition order and no local recourse lower national baseline.
Strong non-discrimination, hate-crime and traveler shield laws reduce local facility/service risk; lack of enforcement data and unchanged national border/passport exposure keep it elevated.

Government/school facility exclusion with complaint system and visitor-unfriendly documentary defence adds exposure; partial protections and no private-sector reach keep it less severe than comprehensive bans.

Comprehensive biological-sex facilities law, sleeping-quarter causes of action, no state hate-crime/non-discrimination, and worst-adult ranking create inescapable state-tolerated exposure; national document/entry risk worsens.
